name: rtx2060
description: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 2060 (TU106, Turing, sm_75) at its 1365 MHz base clock: one Vortex core per SM.

sources.NUM_CORES, NUM_WARPS, NUM_THREADS, ISSUE: 30 SMs (1920 CUDA cores), 32 resident warps per SM (1024 threads, compute capability 7.5), 4 processing blocks each with its own scheduler and L0 instruction cache (NVIDIA Turing architecture whitepaper)
sources.NUM_ALU_LANES, NUM_FPU_LANES, NUM_LSU_LA: TU10x SM processing block: 16 FP32 cores, 16 INT32 cores, 4 LD/ST units, 4 SFUs and 2 tensor cores (Turing whitepaper, Figure 4). One Vortex ALU/FPU/LSU block per processing block with the part's INT32, FP32 and LD/ST lanes. FP64 FMAs run on their own F64 FMA PE (FMA64_PE_RATIO)
sources.FMA64_PE_RATIO: FP64 FMA at 1/32 of the FP32 rate: 2 FP64 cores per SM (CUDA C++ Programming Guide, arithmetic instruction throughput, compute capability 7.5). A block keeps at least one PE, so 16 FPU lanes / 16 = 1 F64 FMA PE per block: 1/16 of FP32, twice the part's FP64 rate
sources.FDIV_PE_RATIO, FSQRT_PE_RATIO, FCVT_PE_R: 16 results per clock per SM, 4 per processing block: FP32 reciprocal and reciprocal square root, on which division and square root are built, and the 32-bit type conversions (CUDA C++ Programming Guide, compute capability 7.5); 16 FPU lanes / 4
sources.DCACHE_SIZE, DCACHE_NUM_WAYS, DCACHE_NUM: 96 KB L1/shared per SM (Turing whitepaper): 6 ways over power-of-two sets, the whole pool as in the other profiles (the driver gives a kernel the L1 its shared memory leaves). 64 B per clock of L1 data per SM, 16 LD/ST units x 4 B (Jia et al., T4, Table 3.2: 58.8 B/cycle/SM measured): 2 banks of the 32 B dcache word
sources.LMEM_SIZE, LMEM_LOG_SIZE: 64 KB maximum shared memory per SM (CUDA Programming Guide, compute capability 7.5)
sources.LMEM_NUM_BANKS: 128 B per clock per SM: 32 banks of 4 B on the part (CUDA C++ Programming Guide, shared memory). Vortex banks are XLEN wide (8 B), so 16 banks carry the same bytes per clock
sources.L2_SIZE, L2_NUM_WAYS, L2_NUM_BANKS: 3 MB L2 (TU106 with 192-bit memory): 24 ways over power-of-two sets; one bank per memory channel
sources.PLATFORM_MEMORY_TYPE, PLATFORM_MEMORY_NU: 192-bit GDDR6 at 14 Gbps: 6 devices x 2 x16 channels = 12 channels, modelled as 16 at 10500 MT/s for a power-of-two interleave: 16 x 2 B x 10.5 GT/s = 336 GB/s, the card's bandwidth
sources.PLATFORM_CLOCK_RATE: 1365 MHz base clock (1680 MHz boost), the clock of Accel-Sim's SM75_RTX2060 configuration
sources.EXT_TCU_ENABLE, TCU_*: Second-generation tensor cores, two per processing block: FP16, INT8 and INT4 (Turing whitepaper); no TF32, BF16 or sparsity
sources.TCU_PE_RATIO: 512 dense FP16 FMA per clock per SM: 8 tensor cores of 64 FMA each (Turing whitepaper). A TCU block at NUM_THREADS=32 computes 256 FP16 FMA per clock, so the 4 blocks give 1024: ratio 2
sources.EXT_RTU_ENABLE: Off although the part has one RT core per SM: the RTU needs full-warp ALU lanes (NUM_ALU_LANES == NUM_THREADS), and the part's 16 INT32 lanes per block take precedence
sources.NUM_MUFU_LANES: 16 special-function results per clock per SM, 4 SFUs per processing block (compute capability 7.5)
sources.VM_ENABLE, EXT_A_ENABLE, EXT_ZACAS_ENABL: As in the other NVIDIA profiles: demand-paged MMU, atomics with CAS, FP16, 16 named barriers, and the graphics pipeline of a GeForce part
sources.CP_LLC_CLIENT: Host copies reach device memory through the L2 like every other client, so uploaded data is L2-resident at launch
sources.reference: fp32_lanes is the vendor FP32 core count (FP32 FMA lanes per chip, clock-free); dram_bandwidth_gbs the vendor peak. Checked by ci/profile_check.py. Latencies: Jia et al., Dissecting the NVIDIA Turing T4 GPU via Microbenchmarking (arXiv 1903.07486), Table 3.1 and Figure 3.5: L1 hit 32, L2 hit 188, L2 miss with a TLB hit 296 cycles on the T4 (TU104), the same Turing SM, L1 and L2 design on GDDR6; Accel-Sim's SM75_RTX2060 configuration is tuned to 32 (L1) and 194 (L2) cycles on this card. Accel-Sim correlates this card (posted hardware runs: turing-rtx2060)
sources.L2_LINK_LATENCY: 64 core cycles each way between an SM and the L2, the SM-to-L2 network, which the L2 bank pipeline (L2_LATENCY) does not model: calibrated with ci/profile_check.py so the SimX pointer chase gives the 188-cycle L2 hit latency in 'reference'
sources.PLATFORM_MEMORY_LATENCY: 37 core cycles of PHY/NoC latency beyond the L2 link, calibrated with ci/profile_check.py so the SimX cold pointer chase gives the 296-cycle global memory latency in 'reference'
sources.L2_MSHR_SIZE: 32 per bank: Little's law on the L2-miss round trip (DRAM 296 - L2 hit 188 = 108 cycles) x 246 B/cycle (336 GB/s / 1365 MHz) / (16 banks x 64 B) = 26, rounded up to a power of two. The derived default counts only PLATFORM_MEMORY_LATENCY, which the link latency mostly replaces
